marks.gloss_en: the baraita (sent back) is where he remembered after 'who hears prayer'
דאמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן: מצוה להתפלל עם דמדומי חמה -- as R' Yochanan said it is a mitzva to pray with the reddening of the sun
מאי קראה -- ייראוך עם שמש ולפני ירח דור דורים
מאי טעמא -- דלמא מיטרפא ליה שעתא: lest the hour slip by him
Abaye bar Avin and R' Chanina bar Avin: [fixed prayer is that of] anyone who does not pray with the reddening of the sun
R' Zeira: I am able to innovate something in it [prayer], and I fear lest I become confused
R' Yehoshua: one who walks in a place of danger prays a short prayer, etc. (the mishnah, cited as the lemma)
one who erred and did not mention the New Moon in the Temple-service blessing returns to the Temple-service blessing
'finished -- returns to the start' was said only where he has uprooted his feet
'uprooted his feet -- returns to the start' was said only where he is not accustomed to say supplications after his prayer
'did not uproot his feet -- returns to the Temple-service blessing' was said only where he is accustomed to say supplications after his prayer
the baraita: one who walks in a place of bands of wild beasts and robbers prays a short prayer
R' Yehoshua: 'Hear the cry of Your people Israel, and quickly do their request. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer'
R' Elazar b. R' Tzadok: 'Hear the outcry of Your people Israel, and quickly do their request. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer'

Acherim: 'The needs of Your people Israel are many and their understanding is short; may it be Your will, Lord our God, to give each one his sustenance and each body what it lacks. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer'
Rav Huna: the halakha follows Acherim
Eliyahu: do not grow angry, and you will not sin

what is the traveller's prayer? 'May it be Your will, Lord my God, that You lead me toward peace, direct my steps toward peace, support me toward peace, rescue me from every enemy and ambush on the way, send blessing in the work of my hands, and grant me grace, kindness and mercy in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see me. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer'
R' Eliezer: whoever makes his prayer fixed -- [his prayer is not supplication] (the mishnah, cited with 'etc.')
